name: Hemoglobin
low_meaning: Low hemoglobin is called anemia. It often causes tiredness, dizziness or breathlessness. Common causes are low iron, heavy periods, or pregnancy needs. A doctor finds the cause.
high_meaning: A high value can come from dehydration, smoking, or living at high altitude. A doctor should review it.

name: TSH (thyroid)
low_meaning: A low TSH can mean an overactive thyroid. The doctor usually confirms with T3 and T4 tests.
high_meaning: A high TSH can mean an underactive thyroid (hypothyroidism). The doctor usually confirms with a T4 test and your symptoms.

name: Fasting blood sugar
low_meaning: A fasting sugar below 70 mg/dL is low and can cause shakiness and sweating. Discuss it with your doctor.
high_meaning: 100 to 125 mg/dL fasting is the prediabetes range. 126 or more on repeat tests can point to diabetes. Only a doctor can confirm.

name: HbA1c
high_meaning: 5.7 to 6.4% is the prediabetes range and 6.5% or more can point to diabetes. A doctor confirms and plans next steps.

name: Ferritin (iron stores)
low_meaning: Low ferritin means low iron stores, even before anemia shows up. Ask about the cause and how to replace iron safely.
high_meaning: High ferritin can occur with inflammation, infection or liver conditions. A doctor should review it.

name: Vitamin D (25-OH)
low_meaning: Below 30 ng/mL is commonly seen as low, and it is very common in India. The doctor decides the dose and duration.
high_meaning: A very high level is usually from too many supplements. Tell your doctor what you take.

name: Vitamin B12
low_meaning: Low B12 can cause tiredness, tingling in hands or feet, and anemia. It is more common if you eat little or no animal food.
high_meaning: A high level is often from supplements. Tell your doctor what you take.

name: Prolactin
high_meaning: High prolactin can cause missed periods, milk discharge when not pregnant, or trouble conceiving. Stress, some medicines, and pregnancy can also raise it.

name: Total cholesterol
high_meaning: 200 mg/dL or more is above the desirable level. Diet and activity help; the doctor may check a full lipid profile.
